title: Bounded derived functors stabilize on the truncation tower

from.place: proof, first step, uniform upper truncation bound

statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $F:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Ab}$ be an additive functor on the category of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with right derived functors $RF$ and $R^pF$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Let $N\geq0$ be an integer and assume $R^pF(\mathcal F)=0$ for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ and every $p\geq N$. Let $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] and, for every integer $n$, put $E_n=\tau_{\geq-n}E$ (standard truncation [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]), with transition maps $E_n\to E_{n-1}$ the canonical ones. Then for all integers $i$ and $n$ with $n\geq N-i$ the induced map $H^i(RF(E_n))\to H^i(RF(E_{n-1}))$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: The proved private helper isZero_rightDerived_shifted_single composes four isomorphisms: the identification of Q of the degree-zero single complex with DerivedCategory.singleFunctor; RF commutation with the n-shift; the cohomology shift isomorphism from degree j of the n-shift to degree n+j; and F.homologyRightDerivedFunctorObjSingleFunctorIso from PlusCompatibility. The latter is the already-proved bounded-below single-object comparison transported by F.rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility. Thus vanishing of R^p F(M), with n+j=p, gives vanishing of H^j(RF(M[0][n])).

source.place: Tag 08D4 proof of part (2), truncation triangle H^{-n}(E)[n] -> E_n -> E_{n-1} and the two shifted vanishings

proof.text: Set M=H^{-n}(E). It is quasi-coherent by E.property (-n). For j=i and j=i+1, the inequality n>=N-i gives n+j>=N>=0. Use p=(n+j).toNat; integer arithmetic proves its cast equals n+j and N<=p. Apply hvan and the preceding helper to obtain the two zero endpoint objects.

proof.text: Use HomologySequence.mono_homologyMap_mor₂_iff and epi_homologyMap_mor₂_iff on the mapped distinguished triangle. The incoming arrow is zero since its source is zero, and the connecting arrow is zero since its target is zero. The middle homology map is therefore monic and epic; isIso_of_mono_of_epi proves the unchanged conclusion.

lean.statement: theorem isIso_rightDerivedFunctor_lowerTruncation_step (X : Scheme.{u}) [HasDerivedCategory.{w₁} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))] [HasDerivedCategory.{w₂} AddCommGrpCat.{u}] [Abelian.HasKInjectiveResolutions (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))] [HasInjectiveResolutions (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))] (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}) [F.Additive] (N : ℕ) (hvan : ∀ (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)), M.IsQuasicoherent → ∀ p : ℕ, N ≤ p → IsZero ((F.rightDerived p).obj M)) (E : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X) (i n : ℤ) (hn : (N : ℤ) - i ≤ n) : IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} i).map (F.rightDerivedFunctor.map ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.natTransTruncGEOfLE (-n) (-n + 1) (Int.le_add_one (le_refl (-n)))).app E.obj)))
